text:
You were promised AI would free up your time. Instead it relocated the problem from your calendar straight into your head 🧠

AI removes the limit on how much you can produce. In an hour you can generate a dozen drafts, analyses, or plans that used to take a week. Reading each one, checking it, and turning it into an actual decision? Still you.

So you attach AI to everything it technically fits, and instead of freeing up time you build yourself a review queue with no bottom. You've become an editor on a conveyor belt that never stops.

Three things that changed how this feels for me:

1️⃣ Get the task right before you touch the prompt. Ask for a twenty-page market analysis when what you really needed was to pick between two vendors, and you'll get twenty genuinely good pages and zero decisions made. The prompt was fine, but the task was wrong. 

This is where most "AI just isn't that smart" complaints actually come from.

2️⃣ AI processes information, you make the decisions. Searching, collecting, structuring, comparing, first drafts, hand all of that over, it's good at it and you'll get hours back 🦾 But picking a direction, weighing trade-offs, deciding what actually matters, that's yours 🫵 

Somewhere around task number 37 of the day, "here's a solid draft" quietly turns into "sure, ship it", and that's the part worth watching for.

3️⃣ You can hand off the work. Not the blame. You sent the proposal, you made the call on your team, you put the AI's recommendation into production. The consequences are yours.

 "AI suggested it" isn't an explanation your client or your boss is going to accept, and it shouldn't be one you accept from yourself either.

My own morning brief pulls tasks out of the previous day's calls and assembles the standup with one command. But it works not because it's fast, it works because it hands me the day as "here are the decisions to make" instead of "here's a pile of material, good luck".

So the real metric isn't how many tools you're running. It's whether your actual day got shorter. If AI added more steps, more queues, more tabs to babysit, that's not a transformation, that's just a fancier mess.

AI isn't the end result. The result is a better way to live and work 🐈

Honestly: since you brought AI in, do you have more free time or more inbound queue? One word in the comments👇
